# LibreBugBounty 2.0.0 Moneta

Moneta turns the original triage prototype into a local workspace for URL
intake, screenshot evidence, manual decisions, and report preparation. Cases
and evidence stay on your machine.

## Highlights

- **A complete workspace:** dedicated Intake, Inventory, Review, Statistics,
  and Export pages. URL intake saves to SQLite before browser work begins,
  detects duplicate URLs, and queues Chromium screenshots persistently.
- **Review built around the screenshot:** the image fits the available window,
  details scroll separately, and fixed controls mirror the arrow keys.
  **→** marks Vulnerable, **←** marks Not vulnerable, **↑** opens the stored URL,
  **Enter / number-pad Enter** skips, and **↓** returns to the previous case and
  resets it to unassessed. Repeated Back includes skipped cases and retains
  notes, contacts, observations, evidence, and judgment history. Reset judgments
  remain auditable and no longer count in effective statistics or export evidence
  selection. An optional three- or five-second decision pause helps avoid
  accidental classifications. Buttons also work without JavaScript.
- **Evidence and decisions kept separate:** later contradictions, inconclusive
  observations, and technical errors can return an assessed case to review
  without replacing your decision. Search cases, record private notes and
  completed contacts, and request rechecks or new screenshots while retaining
  previous evidence.
- **Activity statistics:** follow intake, contacted cases, and manually fixed
  cases over the last three months through today by default, or choose
  weekly, monthly, yearly, all-time, or custom periods, grouped by day, week,
  or month. Includes an activity calendar and domain-suffix breakdowns.
- **Reports for manual sharing:** export compact URL lists, current case-state
  JSON, or ZIP packages containing a readable report, structured domains and
  cases, and selected available screenshots. Private notes are included only
  when selected. Missing or unsuitable images are listed with their reasons.
- **Saved workflow preferences:** choose the initial inventory page size,
  export profile, and report screenshots alongside the intake marker, browser
  timeout, and review pause. Factory defaults are 10 cases per page and a ZIP
  report with the latest stored screenshot per case. Explicit page choices
  take precedence; private notes remain a choice for each export.
- **Local backup and documentation:** the backup tool keeps SQLite and the
  artifact tree together and verifies a separate restoration. English
  documentation is available inside the app offline. The interface defaults
  to English and supports persistent German/English switching.

## Upgrading

Create and verify a complete backup before upgrading. JSON and ZIP reporting
exports do not preserve the complete workspace history.

Stop DDEV and update the checkout, preserving local configuration. If you use
custom storage paths, carry both `DATABASE_URL` and `EVIDENCE_STORAGE_DIR` into
`.ddev/config.yaml` under `web_environment` before restarting. Moneta explicitly
sets these variables there; old `.env` values alone no longer select your storage.
Use container paths in DDEV and the corresponding host paths for the backup tool.

While DDEV is stopped, remove the generated `playwright-worker/node_modules/`
directory if present. The next `ddev start` installs locked dependencies,
applies pending migrations, and starts the screenshot worker. Existing cases
and evidence are retained. Check that your stored workspace is available.

For rollback, restore the matching pre-upgrade database and artifacts into a
separate directory and use the corresponding application version. See
[installation and upgrade](https://github.com/tfgrass/librebugbounty/blob/v2.0.0/README.md#upgrade-an-existing-workspace)
and [backup and recovery](https://github.com/tfgrass/librebugbounty/blob/v2.0.0/BACKUP.md).

## Scope and compatibility

LibreBugBounty remains a local, single-user application focused on reflected
XSS triage. Keep its web and Playwright services local; there is no login or
multi-user permission model. Disclosure emails and report submission remain
manual tasks.

The legacy web interface and HTML report export have been removed. Historical
data and compatibility routes for existing bookmarks remain available through
the current interface. Contact and sent markers remain separate records.

Saved export defaults apply to the Export page. Existing direct
`/export/download` links without a profile still return current-state JSON;
report links without a screenshot choice still use assessment-basis images.
The page's generated download links carry its effective choices explicitly.
